questions.stem: What happens to energy during a chemical reaction?

options.text: Energy remains unchanged in all reactions
Energy is transferred to or from the surroundings
Energy is always destroyed
Energy is always created

questions.explanation: During chemical reactions, energy is transferred between the chemical system and the surroundings. Energy is conserved (not created or destroyed), but it can be transferred as heat to the surroundings (exothermic) or absorbed from the surroundings (endothermic).

options.text: A reaction that transfers energy to the surroundings, causing a temperature increase
A reaction that takes in energy from the surroundings
A reaction that does not involve any energy change
A reaction that only occurs at high temperatures

questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction transfers energy to the surroundings (usually as heat), causing the temperature of the surroundings to increase. The prefix 'exo-' means 'out', so energy goes out to the surroundings.

options.text: A reaction that only occurs in cold conditions
A reaction that releases energy to the surroundings
A reaction that takes in energy from the surroundings, causing a temperature decrease
A reaction that produces light

questions.explanation: An endothermic reaction absorbs energy from the surroundings (usually as heat), causing the temperature of the surroundings to decrease. The prefix 'endo-' means 'in', so energy goes in from the surroundings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an exothermic reaction?

options.text: Photosynthesis
Thermal decomposition
Dissolving ammonium nitrate in water
Combustion (burning)

questions.explanation: Combustion is a common exothermic reaction that releases large amounts of heat and light energy to the surroundings. Photosynthesis, thermal decomposition, and dissolving ammonium nitrate are all endothermic processes.

questions.stem: A student measures the temperature of a solution before and after adding a chemical. The temperature drops from 22°C to 15°C. What type of reaction has occurred?

options.text: Neutralisation
Endothermic
Exothermic
No reaction has occurred

questions.explanation: The temperature decrease shows that the reaction has absorbed heat energy from the solution (surroundings), causing it to cool down. This is characteristic of an endothermic reaction.

questions.stem: How can you measure the energy change in a reaction using a simple calorimetry experiment?

options.text: By measuring the temperature change of the solution using a thermometer
By measuring the mass of the products
By measuring the colour change of the solution
By counting the number of bubbles produced

questions.explanation: A simple calorimetry experiment involves measuring the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution using a thermometer. A temperature rise indicates an exothermic reaction; a temperature fall indicates an endothermic reaction.

questions.stem: Which of the following everyday processes is endothermic?

options.text: Respiration in living cells
Hand warmers generating heat
A cold pack used for sports injuries
Burning natural gas in a boiler

questions.explanation: Cold packs used for sports injuries contain chemicals that undergo an endothermic reaction when mixed, absorbing heat from the surroundings and making the pack feel cold. Burning gas, hand warmers, and respiration are all exothermic.
